---
title: "Installation"
---

## Install the package

`sportsdataverse` is published on PyPI and conda-forge.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### pip

```bash
pip install sportsdataverse
```

### uv

```bash
uv add sportsdataverse
```

### conda

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge sportsdataverse
```

:::

Optional extras pull in the heavier model / test / docs dependencies:

```bash
pip install "sportsdataverse[all]"     # everything
pip install "sportsdataverse[models]"  # NFL / CFB model inference deps
```

## Runtime requirements

- **Python** 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, or 3.14.
- **DataFrame engine:** polars 1.x end-to-end. Every loader accepts
  `return_as_pandas=True` to hand back a pandas frame instead.

## Verify the import

This cell runs at build time and proves the package is importable in the
documentation environment, and reports the installed version:

```{python}
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from importlib.metadata import version
import sportsdataverse as sdv  # noqa: F401

print("sportsdataverse", version("sportsdataverse"))
```

The per-sport namespaces are attributes of the top-level package:

```{python}
sports = ["nba", "wnba", "nfl", "mlb", "nhl", "mbb", "wbb", "cfb", "odds"]
{s: hasattr(sdv, s) for s in sports}
```

Every value above is `True`, so each league's `espn_<sport>_*` loader family is
ready to import. Continue to [Teams & scoreboard](teams-and-scoreboard.qmd).
